## Project Spotlight: Auto Loader vs COPY INTO for Incremental Ingestion

As a data engineer working with Databricks, I've had my fair share of designing and implementing incremental ingestion pipelines. Recently, I worked on a project that involved ingesting 10 million+ patient records daily from various EHR systems into our data lakehouse.

## Context
Our data team needed to ensure that the ingestion process was not only scalable and reliable but also cost-effective. We were evaluating two popular options: Auto Loader and COPY INTO.

## The Problem
The existing ingestion process was using COPY INTO, which was resulting in duplicate records and data inconsistencies. Moreover, it was expensive, with costs ballooning to $10k+ per month. We needed a more efficient and reliable solution.

## The Solution
I decided to experiment with Auto Loader, which provides a simple, scalable, and cost-effective way to ingest data into Delta Lake. I configured Auto Loader to use `cloudFiles` mode with `databricks.cloudFiles.schemaInference` enabled. This allowed us to automatically infer the schema and handle evolving schema changes.

```python
dbutils.fs.cp("s3://my-bucket/incoming-data/", "dbfs:/mnt/patient-records/incoming-data/")
spark.read.format("cloudFiles").option("cloudFiles.schemaInference", "true").load("dbfs:/mnt/patient-records/incoming-data/").write.format("delta").mode("append").saveAsTable("patient_records")
```

## The Impact
By switching to Auto Loader, we achieved:

*   30% reduction in ingestion costs, from $10k+ to $7k+ per month
*   Zero duplicate records and 99.99% data accuracy
*   25% reduction in ETL processing time, from 2 hours to 1.5 hours

## Takeaways
When it comes to incremental ingestion, Auto Loader offers a more scalable, reliable, and cost-effective solution compared to COPY INTO. With Auto Loader, you can easily handle large volumes of data and evolving schema changes.
